name: Grandmaster Flash
hook: Turned two turntables and a mixer into an instrument with its own technique, before hip-hop had a name for what he was doing.
blurb: Born Joseph Saddler, Flash took DJ techniques that had grown up informally at Bronx park jams and made them into a method anyone could repeat and learn. Among them were the quick-mix and the backspin, ways of cutting between two copies of the same record so the crowd never heard the song stop, and punch phrasing. His 1981 record "The Adventures of Grandmaster Flash on the Wheels of Steel" is a recording of that technique itself, mixing Chic, Queen and Blondie live, rather than a song built from it. That is why it is treated as a founding hip-hop record even though it came before most rapping on record.

signatureTracks.title: The Adventures of Grandmaster Flash on the Wheels of Steel
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: A recording of the DJ technique itself: three turntables, no rapping, Flash cutting between Chic, Queen, and Blondie in real time.

signatureTracks.title: The Message (Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Credited to Flash and the group, though written mainly by Melle Mel, Duke Bootee, and Sugar Hill staff; a useful case of a group name carrying more authorship weight than the credits reflect.
